g.text: the architecture that broke open modern AI
2017 — VASWANI ET AL., "ATTENTION IS ALL YOU NEED"

div.style: font-size:24px; line-height:1.4; color:#1f1a14; font-style:italic; font-family:Georgia, serif;

foreignObject.div: Every token in the input is enriched with three layers of information — generic meaning, position, and attention-mixed context from every other token. Once each token carries all that, the model can process them in parallel.

g.text: Words as coordinates in latent space

foreignObject.div: Every token gets mapped to a 256–512-dim vector. The axes below are labeled "animal / bird" for intuition only — real Word2Vec dimensions are learned and uninterpretable. Words with similar contexts end up close together; the cluster structure is the thing, not the axis names.

div.style: font-family:'JetBrains Mono', monospace; font-size:11px; letter-spacing:2px; color:#b8472e; font-weight:700; margin-bottom:12px;

div.p: These coordinates are generic. The vector for dog is identical in:

p.style: margin:0 0 6px; font-family:'JetBrains Mono', monospace; font-size:13px; color:#1f1a14;
margin:0 0 18px; font-family:'JetBrains Mono', monospace; font-size:13px; color:#1f1a14;

div.p: Same words. Opposite meanings. Word2Vec carries no order and no input-specific relationships.

g.text: Vectors illustrative. Real positional encodings use sine/cosine; real attention weights are softmax-normalized rows of the attention matrix.
A matrix of who looks at whom

div.style: font-family:'JetBrains Mono', monospace; font-size:11px; letter-spacing:2px; color:#b8472e; font-weight:700; margin-bottom:12px;

div.p: Each row = one token (the query) and how strongly it attends to every other token (the keys).
Rows sum to 1 — each row is a softmax-normalized probability distribution. (Word2Vec vectors do not sum to 1.)
Numbers illustrative — the real values come from learned Q/K projections.

g.text: ⚠ Strictly serial — hard to use a GPU
✓ Every token sees every other directly
⚠ But: O(n²) compute in sequence length
layers aren't cleanly labeled in practice.)

div.p: Each block consumes the previous block's output, transforms it, and passes it on — same shape, richer content. Like a Spring FilterChain mutating a request object as it flows through.
Same logic as hidden layers in an ANN or successive conv layers in a CNN (edges → parts → objects).
6 is the paper's choice. BERT-base = 12 encoder layers, GPT-3 = 96 decoder layers. Not sacred.
Each sublayer is wrapped in LayerNorm(x + Sublayer(x)) — a residual connection plus normalization. The "add" in the lecturer's diagram is this residual; it's important for training stability.

g.text: → parallel processing on GPU → scale → modern AI.
